notes: muse's /goal <objective> command pins a durable, progress-tracked objective (goal_revisions: status/percent_complete/llm_steps_used/wake_if_idle) and the session keeps working toward it across internal iterations with no further user prompt -- the driver sends exactly ONE slash command for the whole run. Whether the daemon renders the internal iterations as one continuous working span or a fast ready/working flicker per iteration is debounce-window-dependent (see the claudecode and copilot 2-7 siblings, the latter reproducing BOTH shapes live off the identical recipe on the identical adapter across two recordings) -- not a property of muse itself. This spec therefore asserts a sustained-duration working hold rather than a fixed phase count, so it does not flake against whichever shape a given recording produces, and settles once the goal converges (percent_complete reaches 100, which muse's own schema ties 1:1 to status=complete) with no explicit clear/cancel step. muse is a single-birth FilesUnderRoot adapter (stable session id from launch), so the birth phase is unpinned to either the generic proc-<PID> pre-session row or muse's own near-instant UUID session, matching the 1-1 session-start precedent.

text: Session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching
Spec: 'ready → working at loop start' — the single /goal <objective> command drives the first internal iteration

The goal loop keeps iterating internally toward the objective with no further driver input — no fresh user message is sent after loop_start. Asserts only that working activity is sustained for a real interval and the session never gates on waiting; deliberately does not assert a fixed cycle count (see notes: the ready/working boundary between internal iterations is debounce-dependent, corroborated by the copilot 2-7 sibling reproducing both a flickering and a coalesced-continuous shape off the identical recipe).

Spec: 'after the goal is reached: working → ready' — the goal converges to 100% complete and the session settles to ready with no explicit /goal clear/cancel step (no confirmed slash syntax for one; the schema's own 'complete must be exactly 100 percent' constraint ends the loop on convergence).
